stops.note: 'a twelfth part', of a foot or of a pound; the same word later reached English again through French as 'ounce'
borrowed directly from Latin; the laws of King Æthelberht of Kent (c. 600) measure wounds in 'inches'
an English statute traditionally dated to 1324 defined the inch as three barleycorns; since 1959 it has been exactly 25.4 mm by international agreement

current_meaning: a unit of length equal to one twelfth of a foot (2.54 cm)
